newsitem.title: YEMEN: Initial Yemen poll results show ruling party ahead.
newsitem.headline: Initial Yemen poll results show ruling party ahead.

text.p: Yemen's ruling General Peoples Congress (GPC) won 93 constituencies in counting so far and the Islamist Islah party won 16 in the country's first general poll since a 1994 civil war, an election official said on Tuesday.

As of 4 p.m. (1300 GMT), results showed independents had won 24 seats in the 301-seat parliament while other parties won two in Sunday's election, Saeed al-Hekaimi, spokesman for the Supreme Election Committee, told reporters.
Western diplomats have said President Ali Abdullah Saleh's GPC is expected to emerge with a large majority while the Islah, its junior coalition partner, could lose ground.
Diplomats and election observers said Islah could slip because its ministers appeared to have failed to deliver many essential day-to-day services.

The Islamists hold socially sensitive portfolios such as electricity, health and water in one of the Arab world's poorest countries. The GPC controls the key ministries of defence, finance, interior and foreign affairs.

Diplomats said independents appeared poised to make strong gains in the ballot, which was overshadowed by shootings in which nine died and allegations of irregularities. Full results are expected by Thursday.

In united Yemen's first elections in 1993, the GPC won 123 seats in parliament followed by Islah with 62 and the Yemen Socialist Party (YSP), 56. Independents won 47 seats while the rest went to Baathist and Nasserite parties.
